title: A New Heaven and a New Earth

reflections.title: "The Sea Was No More"

reflect.text: In our present world, the ocean often stands between people and keeps them apart. To the apostle John on the island of Patmos, the sea was like a prison wall that cut him off from his friends and work. Oceans also change without warning, shifting from calm water to violent waves. Charles Spurgeon noted that in the world to come, "all mournful change shall be unknown." There will be no painful separations and no sudden storms to wreck our joy, but only unbroken fellowship for God's family.

The sea is also a picture of dread, wild power, and deep unrest. People fear the unknown depths below and the mysteries beyond the horizon. Lashed into foam, the waters seem like proud, untamed power that resists all control, much like a troubled life tossed by danger. In God's new world, all restless turmoil ends. Every dark mystery is cleared away, every proud rebellion against God is overcome, and His people enter unbroken rest and peace.

questions: When life feels restless and uncertain like a stormy sea, how does the promise of God's peaceful kingdom give you comfort?
Who are the loved ones you miss today, and how does the hope of unbroken fellowship encourage you?
reflections.prayer: Lord God, thank you for the promise of a world without painful partings, frightening storms, or restless fears. Help us to trust you when our lives feel troubled and tossed by waves of change. Bring us at last to your peaceful home of unbroken rest and joy. Amen.

reflections.title: "He Will Wipe Away Every Tear"

reflect.text: Right now, we live in a world where both men and women must weep. The miseries that came into the world through sin bring genuine heartbreak, grief, and pain. But Scripture promises that this sorrow will end for believers. In the new creation, God Himself comes to dwell with us, turning our mourning into boundless pleasure like that of a great wedding feast. No one can wipe away tears with such gentle care as the God of love.

Our human minds are far too small to grasp all the beauty God has in store for His people. He promises us an eternity completely cleared of fear, physical pain, and death. Even so, the greatest treasure of heaven is not just that our suffering is gone. The highest joy of that new world is being in the personal presence of Jesus Christ Himself.

questions: What hurts or griefs are you carrying right now that you need to place in God's caring hands?
How does looking forward to being in the personal presence of Jesus change how you view your present trials?
reflections.prayer: Heavenly Father, we thank you that our present tears and pains will not last forever. Comfort our hearts when grief feels heavy, and remind us of the boundless joy waiting for us in your presence. Keep our eyes fixed on Jesus, our greatest treasure and hope. Amen.

reflections.title: "Behold, I Make All Things New"

reflect.text: Our world is sadly battered and worn down by sin, and everything in it needs to be renewed. Only the Lord who created all things in the beginning has the mighty power to remake them out of evil. The Lord Jesus has taken up this great task, and He is fully able to carry it out. He has already started this work by renewing human hearts, and one day He will change our nature and give us new bodies like His own glorious body.

Human history is not an endless, meaningless cycle; it moves in a straight line toward a final goal centered on Christ. Jesus will completely finish God's saving plan and renew the entire creation. We are not fading away into defeat, but moving toward a far brighter life. Knowing this wonderful outcome allows us to walk through every difficulty in our daily lives with strong confidence and gladness.

questions: In what ways have you already seen Jesus working to renew your own heart and thoughts?
How does knowing that history is heading toward Christ's complete victory give you confidence today?
reflections.prayer: Lord Jesus, you are the King who makes all things new. Thank you for working in our hearts today and promising to renew all of creation at the end of time. Help us to live each day with joyful confidence, knowing that our future rests safely in your hands. Amen.
